dedupe_keys.name: cropat us annual 1 km crop area and crop type maps of the conterminous us 1850 2021

description: CropAT-US reconstructs annual crop density and crop type maps for the contiguous United States at 1 km from 1850 to 2021, excluding summer idle or fallow land and cropland pasture. The figshare record says the maps combine multi-source, cross-scale inventories with satellite datasets; the density map gives the fraction of each cell under cultivation and the type map the corresponding crop, filling a gap in long crop type histories for environmental and socio-economic analysis. It was published by Shuchao Ye, Peiyu Cao and Chaoqun Lu, first on 19 May 2023 and as version 2 on 21 February 2024, with files of about 2.2 GB, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0, with national coverage. Caveats: early decades rest on county and state inventories allocated to cells, so detail before the satellite era is modelled. For simulation it gives long crop pattern histories to study how agricultural exposure to drought and floods has shifted, and to drive crop water and nutrient demand in long-run models. Related catalogue records include the half-degree nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizer use data and the USGS modeled crop cover 2000-2013.
